project_title: Technical Photographer/Videographer for Strict Lighting & Angle Requirements

project_metadata.job_title: Technical Photographer/Videographer for Strict Lighting & Angle Requirements
project_metadata.job_description:
I’m looking for a commercial or product photographer in the Las Vegas area to photograph a three‑panel artwork on a tabletop setup and capture a short 4K walkthrough video. This is a simple, controlled, technical shoot.

If you’re comfortable with clean studio lighting and shooting products or tabletop subjects, you’re already in the right zone.

Project details:

Photograph each of the three panels (8x10 inch).

Specific shot list will be provided.

Shoot a short, approximately 20 second 4K walkthrough video of the artwork while displayed on tabletop.

Bring your own lighting (softbox), suitable for tabletop work.

Use a boom arm or overhead setup to shoot straight down (necessary)

Keep all shots perfectly square and level (important for consistency)

Deliver RAW files + your standard edited versions (TIFF or high‑res JPEG)

Requirements:

Must be based in Las Vegas and able to travel to indoor location within the city.

Ability to shoot RAW

Video capability (simple, steady walkthrough) capturing the artwork according to technical requirements which will be provided for clarification prior to shoot.

Session length:  
Approximately 60–90 minutes.

Looking forward to working with a local photographer who can deliver clean, well‑lit, square overhead, and detail shots for artwork documentation.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi John, yes I have a boom arm that can get a 90 degree top-down angle, and soft box to diffuse the lighting... Thanks again, let me know if you have any other questions...

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Great, thanks for confirming you have the boom arm and softbox.

I’ll send over the shot list and the technical requirements for the tabletop video walkthrough. This will outline the overhead 90° setup, lighting, and the short video walk‑through while the piece is displayed. For the documentation, I need to video the three panels individually, and also the three together while they are displayed on the same black velvet tabletop used for the shoot. ( I have the velvet and table). The clips need to be edited together to produce a single 20-40 sec video. Its straightforward. I'm attaching the shot list document for added detail and clairty.

Let me know if you have questions, and we can discuss.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Great, let me study over tonight and get back in the morning with any questions. Thanks John!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Question... How tall is the table top, and the high are the ceilings?...

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Table height is 29 inches, and ceiling height is 8 ft.”

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Added Note: I have a collapsible table that can be used, which can bring the height down to 2 inches off the floor. This will give the flat surface necessary to cover with the black velvet, and plenty of overhead room to comfortably take shots and shoot the video. As long as the boom arm off the tripod locks at 90 degrees it will work well. Ideally the art would be wall mounted for shoot, but since the documentation will take place on tabletop there is the necessity to keep 90 degrees so that the shots are square.
